prompt:
Use case: decisive STYLE TRANSFER.
Redraw the ENTIRE female ink-scroll mage in IMAGE 1 using the actual PROJECT GEM ICON ART of IMAGES 2 and 3. The user explicitly rejected image1 as insufficiently gem-icon styled. Produce a visibly different rendering, not a tiny polish pass.

REFERENCE PRIORITY:
Images2 and 3 are the PRIMARY drawing authority: chunky dark-ink contour, strong sculptural large planes, saturated but controlled body color, decisive lit front planes against deep side shadows, a few broad matte brush strokes. Use exactly that economy and form language across the character and props.
Image1 is ONLY identity/design/pose reference. Preserve her composed ADULT face and slightly lowered THREE-QUARTER LEFT head orientation, teal asymmetrical short bob with ivory forelock, black-jade hair ornament, black/ivory/jade Chinese robe, jade/gold clasp, full-body stance, large continuous ink landscape scroll with two rollers, one large calligraphy brush and broad trailing teal cloth. Keep her adult anatomy and original coverage. No new props or costumes.

TRANSFORM THE SHAPE LANGUAGE:
Rebuild hair as 4 or 5 BOLD sculpted locks, each with a large clean top-light face and one large dark side face. Strong deep teal outline. Lose the narrow strand contouring and smooth anime shine.
Robe and sleeves have FEW LARGE CHISELED PAINTED PLANES following real folds. Larger confident angular-to-curved transitions, deeper charcoal shadow masses and clearer ivory lit faces, substantial silhouette. Replace thin delicate linework with an organic ink contour about 1.5 times stronger, tapering at selected ends. Keep cloth looking like cloth, not crystal or metal.
Teal trailing panels use one broad jade main plane, one dark teal fold plane, one lighter turn — big enough to read at thumbnail scale. No tiny scattered triangle facets.
Rollers, brush handle, brush tuft and gold/jade trims should have the same chunky game-item-icon treatment as reference gems: substantial clean forms, restrained wide bevel-like light faces, very few divisions. Brush tuft = 2 or 3 large tapered ink-black masses plus one quiet cool-gray plane, no fine hairs. Ensure a continuous shaft and correct grip.
Landscape scroll is a thick clear ivory strip with a broad cool-gray back/fold plane. Paint only 2–3 compact broad ink-mountain masses and 2 simple bird silhouettes, like an intentionally simplified hand-painted icon inside the scroll. No fuzzy fine landscape texture or scattered clouds everywhere. Preserve its giant flowing arc and structurally coherent front/back paper turns.
Face and skin stay attractive and gently shaded with ONE broad warm base and ONE subtle warm shadow plane; no angular gem shards across face/skin. Simple graphic green eyes, no realistic iris or tiny highlight clusters.
Adult compact game-character head/body relationship consistent with the project. Do not lengthen the body, make the head smaller, alter her gentle expression, hide both eyes or turn back to a profile.

CRITICAL BALANCE:
Stronger geometric volume and big matte hand-painted shapes like the gem references, with LOW DETAIL DENSITY. Each material has about 3 main value groups. Broad quiet areas, clear silhouette. No stained-glass mosaic, countless triangles, low-poly tessellation all over the body, noise, fine grain, micro-brush speckles, metallic glitter, glowing edges, photoreal crystals or 3D render. Do not interpret 'gem style' as adding gems to costume. Do not simply posterize or blur the old image. Repaint cleanly.
Keep original jade/teal, ivory, charcoal-black and muted gold palette, increasing color/value clarity without importing blue or purple colors from style references.
ONE complete full-body figure, entire scroll, brush and both boots inside square plain warm-ivory canvas with clear margin. No background scenery, frame, title, labels, signature, watermark or multiple panels.
purpose: Full redraw from actual project gem-icon references, strengthening broad painted planes and ink contours while preserving the selected head direction and character design.
